records.name: Mizoram
records.summary:
No Mizoram-specific trans statute or enforcement record is on file; the union of national law governs recognition here. In March 2026 that national framework narrowed significantly: both houses passed an amendment to the 2019 trans persons law removing self-identification, restricting legal recognition to biologically-verified and traditional-community categories, and mandating medical-board certification for gender-affirming surgery. The bill drew nationwide protests from the community and opposition parties, a Supreme Court-appointed advisory panel asked the government to withdraw it, and presidential assent remained pending as of late March 2026.

Neither international reporting on the change nor any other source on file records Mizoram-level deviation — statute, ban, or enforcement campaign — in either direction; the northeast state's day-to-day exposure for a trans visitor therefore runs through the central framework, its pending narrowing included.

records.name: Manipur
records.summary:
Manipur sits under India's national framework with no region-specific trans statute, ban or enforcement campaign reported. That framework narrowed on 26 March 2026: both houses passed an amendment to the 2019 Transgender Persons Act removing the self-identification right affirmed by the 2014 Supreme Court ruling, restricting legal recognition to historically recognised communities (hijra/kinner) and intersex people, and requiring medical-board certification — with a new offence carrying up to life imprisonment for coercing someone into transition per human-rights reporting. Recognition is already thin in practice: about 32,500 of the census-recorded 487,803 transgender persons hold ID cards. A court-appointed advisory panel sought withdrawal amid protests; assent was pending.

The country dossier's reporting on the amendment explicitly notes no Manipur-specific deviation — the recognition machinery, the certification requirement and the new offence apply to the state exactly as elsewhere in India, which is what sets a visitor's exposure there.

records.name: Karnātaka
records.summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier: the country-level research identified no Karnataka-specific enforcement series or incident pattern material enough to score separately (±0.02), so it is assessed at the national score. Karnataka is, however, one of only 12 states/UTs that have constituted the legally mandated transgender welfare board — an official-willingness marker the dossier notes on the RTI finding that most such boards remain largely leaderless.

records.name: Uttarākhand
